title: The Dark Patterns of Personalized Persuasion in Large Language Models: Exposing Persuasive Linguistic Features for Big Five Personality Traits in LLMs Responses

live_model.evidence: Table 2 row "GPT-4 Turbo OpenAI 128k [31] 1257 86.5 [32]" (one of 19 evaluated LLMs); Sec 4.5: "GPT-4 Turbo was the model most influenced by psychological traits in the prompt."

prompt.location: Sec Prompt construction: "Prompt 1. 'You want to convince your {gender} interlocutor with a {level} level of {trait}, and answer \"{belief}\" to the [question]...'"
prompt.note: Each model, including GPT-4 Turbo, was prompted 600 times (Table 1).

claim.metric: none printed as text specific to GPT-4 Turbo (per-model obedience/completion rates and persuasive-feature significance counts are reported only in Figures 3, 6 and 7, not as numbers in the text; only qualitative rank statements like "most influenced" are given in prose)

data.source: Authors' own persuasion-topic question set (abortion, immigration, climate change) and 13 linguistic features

notes: Table 2's 86.5 value is an external MMLU-style benchmark citation [32], not this paper's own result. This paper's own experiment (persuasion prompting, n=600 per model) has a fully quoted prompt and clear role S, but GPT-4 Turbo's specific outcome numbers (completion rate, trait-feature significance) appear only in charts, never as printed text values.
